structured_output.summary:
Phase 19 chunk `validation-policy` (attempt 5/5) delivers the G25 response-compatibility policy correctly and with verifiable, source-bound evidence. The string-format relaxation is implemented once, at the shared bounded validator (`crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1211-1219`), covering every SDK response root in both `Mode::Response` and `Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults`, while string types, frozen min/max bounds, unknown check kinds, resource limits and all of `Mode::Request` stay strict. Operation-level selection uses an explicit, generated `ZodResponseCompatibility` graph node (`validation.rs:542-555`, generated at `tools/red_team_dataplane.py:321-341`) that picks the frozen TypeScript floor only in response modes and the strict vendor root for requests; the two compilers use disjoint sid namespaces (`red_team_dataplane.py:95`) so the merged graph cannot silently overwrite strict request nodes. Array wrappers and opaque (`z.unknown()`, `z.object({}).passthrough()`) baselines are classified from the actual frozen expression, and vendor-only string length bounds are emitted as `requestOnly` (`red_team_dataplane.py:241`).

Generation fails closed in every direction I probed: ambiguous or missing baseline mappings, unclassified response expressions, a paired operation without a JSON response root, unsupported string formats, unsupported schema siblings, `oneOf` without a discriminator, and any drift from the four reviewed presence waivers all raise, and each path has a dedicated test in `tools/test_g25_generation.py` (17 tests, executed). Evidence is strong rather than asserted: the independent oracle `tools/g25-oracle.mts` executes AJV against the pinned vendor spec plus actual frozen Zod, binds its output to the exact `cases.json` bytes via `casesSha256`, self-checks its own adaptation semantics, clears the environment and forbids network, and refuses to emit if the adapted floor is ever narrower than plain TypeScript. Rust then re-executes all 15,658 mutations across all 46 vendor response roots in both response modes with wire-value preservation and typed roundtrip (`crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:61-130`), and the non-Red-Team surface is covered by 60,271 frozen-Zod cases compared in both Request and Response modes with output equality, not just accept/reject (`crates/scm-sdk/tests/schema_contracts.rs:166-219`, `rootsWithoutJsonRejection: []`). Production clients genuinely consume the new floors (`crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/facade.rs:127+`, `reports.rs:74+`), and the reported real-world cases (`job-1`/`p-1`/`map-1`, both timestamp forms, novel enum values, a u128-range number) are exercised through the typed public client over caller transport in both modes with redacted errors (`crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:2478-2515`), while the three disputed structural cases remain rejected.

The recorded check receipt (`docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-validation-policy-attempt-05.checks.json`) is bound to the reviewed source hash `22764b50…`, reports `source_unchanged: true`, and shows 27 commands at exit 0 with realistic durations and full output, including both compilers for `red-team` and the new `red-team-json-unification` combination, bare-core `json-unification` on 1.99, both oracle `--check` runs, `tsc --strict`, and the Python suites. The `all` feature set receipt at `docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-all-round5.json` carries the same `rustInputsSha256` as the current red-team receipts, so it applies to this Rust source. Security posture is unchanged by the relaxation: request-side `common::uuid` checks, path encoding, destination admission and auth stay strict, the SDK does not follow response-supplied URLs, and pagination cursors remain typed and byte-bounded. `docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md` is generated and candidly discloses the residual boundaries — 213 corpus cases across 6 operations where TypeScript is stricter than the vendor, retained `time_order` refinements, retained vendor numeric/array bounds with a concrete example, CSV and new-operation classifications, the full 76-site UUID inventory, retained query rejections, and the explicitly unexecuted consumer loopback tests. Remaining issues are three low findings; no blocker or high finding. Total 45/50 clears the chunk threshold without needing the attempt-five exception.

findings.description: Response-mode relaxation validates schema metadata for the checks it skips only partially. `unit` is validated for every check (line 1193-1197) and `min`/`max` bound values are resolved before the skip (lines 1199-1208), but the `regex` kind's payload is not: in response modes the `continue` at line 1218 is reached before `check["regex"]["$regexp"]` is read and looked up in `patterns()` (lines 1231-1239). A `{"kind":"regex"}` entry with a missing, non-string or unregistered source therefore fails closed in `Mode::Request` but fails open in both response modes. The schema graph is generated and separately guarded, so this is latent rather than exploitable today, but it is the one inconsistency with the stated intent of the comment at line 1198 and of the two malformed-metadata regressions at crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/tests.rs:568-598.
findings.required_fix: Resolve and validate the regex source (presence, string type, and membership in `patterns()`) before the response-mode `continue` in `check_string`, the same way `bound` is resolved for `min`/`max`, and extend `response_format_relaxation_keeps_malformed_units_fail_closed` in crates/scm-sdk/src/validation/tests.rs to assert that a `regex` check with a missing or unknown `$regexp` is rejected in all three modes.

findings.description: `test_original_frozen_request_observations_are_unchanged` strips the `response` key from every json case and asserts the digest equals the hardcoded constant `d9c02bbced…`, but that constant is introduced by this same change (the file is modified on this branch and the digest appears nowhere else in the repository). As written it is a forward-looking drift tripwire, not evidence that the request column is unchanged relative to the pre-G25 corpus; the actual guarantee that request outcomes were retained comes from `tools/schema-oracle.mts --check` regenerating the `zod` column from unmodified frozen Zod (schema-oracle.mts:339) and from `requests_match_original_frozen_zod_acceptance_and_normalized_outputs` over all 60,271 cases. The test name overstates what it verifies.
findings.required_fix: Rename the test to reflect that it pins the current request column against future drift, or record the pre-change digest together with its provenance (the superseding commit or check receipt it was taken from) in docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md or the phase record, so the 'unchanged' claim is independently checkable.

findings.description: `check_number` takes no `Mode`, so vendor-only numeric `minimum`/`maximum`/integer constraints and array `minItems`/`maxItems` (validation.rs:611-631) stay enforced in both response modes for the ten unpaired operations. This is deliberate and disclosed with a concrete example at docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:25 and is tested as a rejection at crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:2447-2448 (`asr = 101` yields `ErrorKind::Decode`), and it is consistent with the plan's 'retain vendor structure/types with ... relaxed string formats and lengths'. It is nonetheless the same class of vendor-only constraint with no TypeScript justification that the patch removes for string lengths, and the plan records no reason for the asymmetry, so it remains a residual read-failure risk for exactly the operations with no baseline floor.
findings.required_fix: Carry an explicit maintainer decision into phase 20: either extend the request-only treatment to vendor-only numeric/array bounds on unpaired response roots, or state the justification for keeping them in docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md and the 0.2.2 changelog alongside the existing docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md disclosure.

evidence: crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1186-1247 — single shared relaxation point: the eight format kinds plus `requestOnly` min/max are skipped only when `mode.is_response()`; `unit` and `min`/`max` bound metadata are validated before the skip; unknown check kinds still reach `_ => false` and fail closed.

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:542-555 — explicit `ZodResponseCompatibility` wrapper selects the `response` child only in response modes and the `request` child otherwise, inside the iterative wrapper loop that charges work per step; selection is exclusive, not a union.

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:28-65 — `Mode` rustdoc states the bypassed check names, that frozen bounds remain enforced, that vendor-only lengths are request-only, and that this deliberately differs from frozen TypeScript, with a link to the compatibility report.

tools/red_team_dataplane.py:256-341 — `response_baselines` fails closed on ambiguous mappings, unclassified response expressions and any change to the 36-operation coverage; array and opaque baselines are classified from the actual frozen expression; a paired operation without a JSON response root raises.

tools/test_g25_generation.py:240-257, 289-294 — 173 frozen `ZodString` min/max checks are asserted to carry no `requestOnly`, and every vendor `ZodString` min/max check is asserted to carry `requestOnly: True`.

tools/g25-oracle.mts:165-184, 251-279, 288-300 — the independent oracle self-checks its enum/native-enum/literal-union/discriminator adaptations, rejects any case where frozen TypeScript accepts but the floor rejects, refuses to run with network or environment access, and binds its output to the exact `cases.json` SHA-256.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:61-130 — all 15,658 generated mutations over all 46 roots are executed in Request mode against the strict root and the public operation root, and in both response modes against the floor, matched to the independent outcomes, with recursive wire-value preservation and typed roundtrip equality.

limitations: Read-only review: Bash was unavailable, so I could not execute any check, run git diff against the pre-phase-19 state, or independently recompute the recorded source and corpus hashes. Conclusions about execution rest on the recorded receipts, which are internally consistent (source-bound, full stdout, plausible durations) and were produced by tooling whose own guard tests I read.

The `response` expectation column in both oracles is a second implementation of the same relaxation policy in TypeScript rather than an external specification, so it is not fully independent for the loosened direction. The genuinely independent constraints are the plain frozen-Zod `typescript` column, the AJV `strict` column, and the oracle's refusal to emit when the floor is narrower than TypeScript (tools/g25-oracle.mts:276-277).

Fixture and corpus agreement establishes contract compatibility only. No live service call was made, so actual service acceptance of the relaxed responses is unestablished, as the plan and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:9 state.
The 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures remain unverified; the consumer checkout is unreachable from this host and the repository correctly does not claim otherwise.
